confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of session hijacking followed by massive cross-departmental data exfiltration. The mid-session IP change is a definitive indicator of hijacking, and the subsequent bulk downloads of sensitive files from departments outside the user's scope (Legal, HR, Engineering, DevOps, Finance, Sales) confirm unauthorized access and exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: User_09 logs in successfully from their normal IP (192.168.1.109).
Session hijacking occurs: the same session_id (sess_user_09_20260404_001) is used from a new, external IP (176.10.99.200), and the user begins accessing files outside their department (/data/logs/).
Unauthorized access and exfiltration begins with the download of a legal configuration file.
Bulk exfiltration continues across multiple departments including Sales, HR, Engineering, DevOps, and Finance.
The attacker logs out from the hijacked session.

gaps: Geographic location of the hijacking IP (176.10.99.200) to confirm it is not a known VPN/travel IP for user_09.
Logs from the authentication provider to see if MFA was bypassed or if a session token was stolen.
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred where user_09's session was hijacked mid-session, evidenced by a sudden IP change from 192.168.1.109 to 176.10.99.200. The attacker used this hijacked session to perform a massive bulk download of sensitive files across nearly every department in the organization, including legal, hr, engineering, and finance data.
